Issued at 211 AM CDT Thu Sep 24 2026

As of 06Z, the shortwave is currently positioned over northwestern 
SD through ND/Canada with winds out of southwest through 850mb and 
southerly/southeasterly winds at the surface. With this flow lots of 
moisture is being pulled in from the south and southwestern US (seen 
on water vapor imagery) in thanks to a 30kt LLJ over much of the CWA 
as the surface trough currently extends just west of the CWA. This 
has led to better coverage and formation of scattered rain showers 
tracking northeast along and just east of the Mo River with 
additional rain moving in from southern SD/NE. 500 j/kg of MUCAPE 
and 25-30kts of bulk shear is producing weak embedded thunderstorms 
we well. Through 12Z CAMs really indicate this shortwave energy 
induced rain across NE/KS continuing to merge with the rain over the 
Northern Plains to produce additional development and better 
coverage of the scattered rain, and potentially weak thunderstorms, 
east of the James River into MN. The last of precip is forecast to 
exit far eastern SD/MN by the midday or early afternoon as CAMs 
overall agree on this. A few of the CAMS do indicate lingering 
spotty showers possible Coteau eastward 18Z through tonight. 
Probability of QPF (or additional QPF)>0.25" (starting at 06Z) is 60-
95% James Valley and eastward, highest along and east of I29. Prob 
for a half inch is 60-80% along and east of I29. Any stronger rain 
showers or storms could produce locally higher QPF. 

Otherwise, dry air aloft moves in behind the system and will 
continue to spread eastward across the CWA with the driest air along 
and west of the MO River by this evening/overnight as the Northern 
Plains remains under this broad ridge and mid level high moves in 
over the region. Surface winds will be out of the southeast/east 
over central SD and southeast over northeastern SD/MN. With ongoing 
low level moisture and cloud cover hanging around, this could result 
in low stratus/drizzle/fog late tonight through Friday morning as 
NAM/EC soundings indicate this classic drizzle setup with some 
omega at the surface to 850 and dry air aloft. So fog and drizzle 
may need to be added in closer to time if confidence increases.

We continue with this shortwave train as more energy moves in from 
the south combining with a stronger negatively tilted shortwave 
moving in from the southwest (per an ongoing trough hanging over the 
PacNW). This neg tilted shortwave will track northeast across the 
region Friday through Saturday. Southeasterly flow at low levels 
will pull in moisture resulting in another round of rain. As of now, 
pops will increase south to north across the CWA Friday afternoon 
and evening with the bulk of the precip occurring Friday night 
through Saturday morning (mainly east of Mo River) with the help of 
strengthening LLJ. Latest NBM pops range from 40-70%, highest James 
Valley and eastward. Rain will diminish west to east through late 
Saturday afternoon. Probability of 24 QPF>0.25 ending Saturday 
evening is 40-60% James Valley and eastward. Still a bit of a 
difference between models QPF wise with the 25-75th spread of 0.3 to 
0.6", highest over eastern and southeastern CWA.

Dry conditions for Sunday but we will continue in this active weather 
pattern as the trough that has been hanging out over the PacNW will 
track northeast into Canada with another trough developing over the 
western CONUS Monday and track eastward and over the central/southern 
CONUS Tuesday/Wednesday. Still quite the difference between the 
Clusters on location timing and intensity and its surface low that 
is forecast to develop over the Northern Rockies and track across 
the Northern Plains Monday/Tuesday bringing the return of rain.
